headline: China Powers Up Massive Solar Plant With Heat-Storage Innovation
meta_description: China switches on its first 1 GW solar plant using 1.9 million panels and molten salt storage to generate electricity after sunset.
summary_short: China has activated a groundbreaking 1 GW solar facility that stores energy in molten salt, enabling electricity generation long after the sun sets.
body:
China has switched on its first 1 gigawatt solar plant, marking a significant leap in renewable energy storage technology. The facility combines 1.9 million solar panels with 10,310 mirrors that concentrate sunlight to heat molten salt inside a 219-metre tower—a system that allows the plant to continue generating electricity after sunset.

Traditional solar farms face a fundamental challenge: the sun doesn't always shine when demand peaks. This installation solves that problem through thermal storage. The heated molten salt acts as a battery of sorts, retaining energy long enough to power the grid through evening hours and into the night.

The scale of the project underscores China's commitment to scaling renewable energy beyond simple photovoltaic arrays. By combining solar collection with heat storage, the plant demonstrates how innovation in energy infrastructure can help nations transition away from fossil fuels while meeting real-world electricity demands.
quick_facts: 10,310 mirrors heat molten salt in tower
